classification.difficultyReason: Combines selecting an umpire, dividing unlabelled teams and subtracting forbidden team allocations.

content.prompt: Nine players are to be divided into two teams of four and one umpire.

children.label: a
children.prompt: In how many ways can the teams be formed?

answer.worked:
Choose the umpire, then divide the remaining eight players into two unlabelled teams of four. Divide by two to avoid counting each split twice.
$$N={}^9C_1\times\frac{{}^8C_4}{2}=315.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If two particular people cannot be on the same team, how many different combinations are possible?

answer.worked:
Subtract allocations with the two particular people on the same team. For these allocations, choose the umpire from the other seven people and choose two of the remaining six to join the particular pair. The other four form the second team.
$$\begin{aligned}N_{\text{same}}&={}^7C_1\times{}^6C_2\times{}^4C_4\\&=7\times15\times1\\&=105\\N_{\text{allowed}}&=315-105\\&=210\end{aligned}$$
